title: Drilling Holes for Electrical Wiring in Studs: Tools, Clearances, and Wire-Pulling Techniques
summary: This Old House's Tool Lab video explains practical methods for boring holes in wood studs to run electrical wiring. It compares auger bits with self-feeding tops, spade bits, and a suite of accessories (extensions, right-angle adapters, flexible bits) to reach tight corners. The presenter emphasizes code-driven clearance from stud edges (minimum 1-1/4 inches) and suggests a center-spotting approach by stepping bit sizes to avoid precise centering on every stud. The workflow covers drilling demonstrations, corner access strategies, and wire-pulling techniques that keep wires at a consistent height, bend wires within the wall bay to form curves, and manage offsets with pre-fitting or “fish” methods. The video also notes protective measures like nail plates when clearance cannot be met and advises checking local codes for multiple cables.

sections.title: Tools and bit options for drilling holes
sections.description: Introduces drill-bit options for boring holes through studs, highlighting the auger bit for high-volume drilling with a self-feeding top bit, and the spade bit for a few clean holes. Mentions accessories to access tight spaces, including extensions, a right-angle adapter, and flexible bits.

sections.title: Clearance rules and hole sizing strategy
sections.description: States the code-required clearance from the edge of a stud (minimum 1-1/4 inches) and explains using smaller bit sizes to approximate the center rather than measuring each stud precisely. Notes that 2x6 studs still allow space considerations and provides practical guidance on where to drill.

sections.title: Auger drilling demonstration and center reference
sections.description: Demonstrates drilling with an auger and using a reference point on the leg to maintain a consistent height and spacing for multiple holes, aiding alignment and planning.

sections.title: Corner access and multiple-extension strategies
sections.description: Explores options when a corner bay is tight: using larger bits, stacking extensions, and pre-fitting through an existing hole to square up to the stud for a clean final hole.

sections.title: Wire-pulling technique and maintaining height
concepts: keeping wires at the same height
bending inside the bay to form a curve
sections.description: Shows how to pull the wire after drilling, emphasizing uniform height to prevent tangling and demonstrates bending the wire against the back wall to create a curve so it navigates corners more easily.

sections.title: Corner offsets, start tricks, and protective measures
concepts: taping a short curve to ease threading
checking local code for multiple cables
sections.description: Addresses off-center or offset corners with a short curve wire (fish method) to start threading and demonstrates protective nail plates when edge-clearance limits are encountered. Reminds viewers to consult local inspectors for cable counts and code allowances.
